title: Windows and macOS platform edge cases

findings.title: macOS: any app's Secure Keyboard Entry is reported as "a system dialog (such as a password prompt) is open"; the accurate reason can never be shown
findings.scenario: Terminal's Secure Keyboard Entry (often enforced on CIS-hardened Macs), a password field left focused, or an app that crashed with secure input on, makes IsSecureEventInputEnabled() true. Ember then refuses every mouse and keyboard action and every screenshot, and the user and model are told "A system dialog (such as a password prompt) is open on the user's screen ... wait" or "(No screenshot: a system dialog is open, so Ember looks away)". No dialog exists, and waiting never helps. The settings setup check has no Secure input row (inspectMac in environment.ts); only `--doctor` names the holder.
findings.evidence: darwin/windows.ts:218-226 makes systemDialogOpen() return true whenever secure().on !== false. withCursor (worker.ts:3095-3099) and perceive (perception/index.ts:415) call that before borrow.begin(), so CursorBorrow's x.blockedReason() (borrow.ts:334), which returns secureInputReason(app) ("Secure keyboard entry is on in Terminal ... until it's off"), is never reached. I bundled darwin/windows.ts with a fake desktop where only secure input is on (secureInput()=true, holder pid 777 = Terminal, no security windows): systemDialogOpen() returned true and secureInput() returned {on:true,pid:777,app:"Terminal"}.
findings.fix: Make the platform answer with a reason, not a bare boolean: systemDialogOpen(): null | string, or add `systemDialogReason()`. Use "Secure keyboard entry is on in <app>" in the worker denial and the no-screenshot note. Alternatively check input.blockedReason() before the generic dialog gate. Add a Secure input row to inspectMac so the settings setup check shows it too.

findings.title: Command and prompt windows are excluded from capture, so remote-access software and screen magnifiers that capture the desktop cannot show them
findings.scenario: createCommandWindow (line 67) and createPromptWindow (line 93) call setContentProtection(true) on Windows and macOS, so these windows are excluded from capture. Electron 44's own docs say a Remote Desktop client still shows such a window, but "remote access software that works by capturing the desktop cannot". Someone using Ember over TeamViewer, AnyDesk, Quick Assist or VNC, or on macOS through Screen Sharing, or with a capture-based magnifier, sees nothing where the command card or the SSH password/consent card should be. That is where commands are approved and secrets typed. The card still reports "whole command in view" to main, because the page's visibility is true locally. The relevant documented limits (L11) rely on this protection and do not mention the downside.
findings.evidence: node_modules/electron/electron.d.ts:6140-6159 documents the behaviour and the Chromium feature `AllowWindowCaptureExclusionInRemoteSessions` that turns it off. Perception already blacks out Ember's own windows by their stack frames (ownWindows/coveringRects), so for Ember's own screenshots the protection is belt and braces. The platform knows the session kind (win32 environment sessionKind: console/rdp/service) but nothing uses it here. Not verified against a real remote tool.
findings.fix: Decide deliberately: either keep protection and document in COMMANDS-WSL-SSH.md that these windows cannot be seen through screen-capture remote tools, or turn the Chromium feature off (or skip setContentProtection) when SM_REMOTESESSION or a remote session is detected. Optionally show a one-line hint in the bubble when the card cannot be seen.

findings.title: macOS: Apple apps on non-English systems are not found by localized name, and a window opened by open_app is not recognised
findings.scenario: On a German or French Mac the window owner name of Apple's own apps is localized ("Rechner", "Systemeinstellungen"). The catalogue only knows the bundle file name ("Calculator", "System Settings"), CFBundleName, the executable and the bundle id, and never reads the localized InfoPlist.strings. open_app("Rechner") finds nothing. open_app("Calculator") launches the app, but worker.ts:1141 compares AxWindow.app against `programs`, so the new window never matches. After 10 s the tool answers "Started Calculator, but its window hasn't appeared yet. Use list_windows and switch_window", and the task has to recover by hand.
findings.evidence: Read: bundleApp() builds `name = path.basename(bundle)` (line 94) and `programs: uniqueLower([name, bundleName, exe, bundle id])` (line 107), using only Info.plist keys, with no lproj lookup. The types.ts contract and the comment in bundleApp say the sidecar's `app` and the window owner are the localized name. worker.ts:1139-1146 matches new windows by programs or by `x.name.includes(app.name)`. Could not run on a localized Mac.
findings.fix: When listing a bundle, also read Contents/Resources/<preferred lproj>.lproj/InfoPlist.strings (CFBundleDisplayName, CFBundleName) with the existing plist reader, and add those names to `keywords` and `programs`.

findings.title: Wayland session is explained but never refused: Ember starts anyway through XWayland and greets as if it works
findings.scenario: RHEL 8's default login is GNOME on Wayland. The launcher always forces --ozone-platform=x11 (packaging/ember:25), so Ember runs against XWayland. The only effect of environment.ts:147-151 failing the "session" check is a row in the settings window and in `ember doctor`; start-up just logs app.ready with failing:["session"]. Ember then shows its greeting ("I'll stay by your cursor ..."), registers shortcuts, and reads and captures through XWayland (root pointer, XTest and XGetImage only see X11 clients). With "Start Ember when I log in" turned on from an earlier Xorg session, a Wayland login gives no explanation at all, because settings is not opened.
findings.evidence: Ran `electron . --doctor --ozone-platform=x11` under Xvfb with XDG_SESSION_TYPE=wayland and WAYLAND_DISPLAY set: the Desktop session row FAILs with the fix text, and the process exits 1. Ran the app itself with --show-settings in the same environment and took a screenshot: it starts normally, logs the failing checks and shows "needs a couple of things fixed", but only below the consent card. Nothing at start-up refuses or interrupts, and nothing in greet() looks at env.checks.
findings.fix: When the session check fails, have greet() say so ("This is a Wayland session ...: log out and choose GNOME on Xorg") and stay out of tier-3 and screenshot work, or exit with startupFailed()'s dialog when the session type is wayland and the check fails. At minimum open settings on every start while a check is failing, even with --autostart.

findings.title: macOS: after every update the ad-hoc-signed Ember asks for the login keychain password, can freeze Ember while it waits, and Deny silently signs the user out; README's update steps do not mention it
findings.scenario: The stored GitHub token is encrypted with Electron's safeStorage, whose key lives in the login Keychain under an access list tied to the app's code identity. Ember is signed ad hoc, which the README says is a new identity on every build. After the user drags a new Ember.app over the old one, the first start (or the first login start) makes macOS show "Ember wants to use your confidential information stored in ... Safe Storage". decryptString() is synchronous on the main process, so the overlay, hotkeys and Stop are unresponsive until the user answers. Choosing Deny or Cancel makes decryptString throw, load() catches it and returns null, and Ember silently shows "not connected". The README update section lists only the TCC permissions (Accessibility, Screen Recording, Input Monitoring).
findings.evidence: auth.ts:37-45: `load()` wraps `this.box.decryptString(raw)` in try/catch and returns null. startBrain calls resolveToken(tokens, ...) on the main thread (main.ts around line 1540). docs/DEVELOPING.md:894 confirms the token is encrypted with a key in the login Keychain. PLAN.md and README say an ad-hoc signature is a new identity to macOS on each build. The prompt itself is standard behaviour for ad-hoc-signed Electron apps that use safeStorage; I could not run a Mac.
findings.fix: Document the keychain prompt next to the TCC re-grant steps in README ("choose Always Allow"). Read the token off the critical path (after the window and overlay are up, with a short "waiting for the keychain" status) and, when decryption throws, say "macOS didn't let Ember read its saved sign-in; sign in again" instead of the generic not-connected state.

findings.title: "Tell the Ember team." is a non-actionable fix for mixed display scaling
findings.scenario: A Windows user with monitors at different scaling sees a warning that Ember "may click in the wrong place on some monitors. Tell the Ember team." There is no contact, issue link or workaround in the app or README, and the user cannot act on it.
findings.evidence: Text at environment.ts:242 and doctor.ts:98 (fix: "Tell the Ember team."); README.md has no support or issue-tracker pointer.
findings.fix: Give a workaround and a place: "Set all monitors to the same scale in Settings › System › Display, then restart Ember. If you can't, report it at <issues URL>." Add that URL to the README.

findings.title: Windows microphone: no setup-check row or button although the code says there is one; the doctor path names Windows 11 only
findings.scenario: A Windows user whose 'Let desktop apps access your microphone' is off (common on managed PCs) turns on 'Hey Ember'. The Voice line says 'Not working: Ember wasn't allowed to use the microphone. To allow it, open the microphone's privacy settings in Settings.' with no button there. main.ts:1583 says 'the setup check has a button for it', and WIN32_FIX_IDS includes open-microphone-settings, but inspectWindows() never emits a microphone check, so the button appears nowhere (the row exists only in the CLI doctor). If Chromium reports that block as NotReadable, micHelp() says 'in use by another app'. The doctor and README give 'Settings › Privacy & security › Microphone', which is the Windows 11 wording; Windows 10 22H2 (supported) says 'Privacy › Microphone'.
findings.evidence: app/main/environment.ts:224-255 (no microphone check for win32); app/main/platform/win32/system/environment.ts:43 (fix id with no producer); app/main/main.ts:1583-1585; app/main/platform/win32/system/doctor.ts:77-79; README.md:44.
findings.fix: Add a Windows 'Microphone' check (warn with fix 'open-microphone-settings') when getMediaAccessStatus is denied/restricted, and a button next to the Voice error. Word the path for both Windows versions ('Settings › Privacy (Privacy & security on Windows 11) › Microphone').
